Subject: RE: Model shortlist + pilot sizing (compatibility + peaks)

Hi team — sharing the proposed shortlist and sizing assumptions below. Attached is a CSV compatibility matrix and an hourly peak workbook so you can plug in alternate concurrency numbers.

Summary (3 model tiers)
- Tier A (cost-optimized): redwood-lite-3B-quant — good for short-turn interactions, p50 ~60ms additional overhead, recommended for help-desk shorthand and quick lookups. Use when input + expected output <= 1.5k tokens.
- Tier B (balanced): redwood-chat-13B-fp16 — standard for mixed workloads, handles up to ~6k total context comfortably with moderate cost. Target for the majority of pilot traffic.
- Tier C (high-context): redwood-long-70B-q4 — for the long multi-turn threads and retrieval-augmented flows where you want full 6k+ token context and highest quality. Reserve for canary or fallback to avoid blowouts.

Context strategy recommendations
- Prefix caching for common prompts (templates, system messages) + KV cache enabled on Tier B/C when session length exceeds 2k tokens. This gives the largest latency win for multi-turn while preserving correctness.
- For very long threads (>4k), use chunked retrieval + condensed system prompt to keep effective context under 6k; flag those requests for async fallback if latency target is strict.

Throughput / token estimate (pilot baseline — assumptions at 30% of expected final traffic):
- Avg tokens per lightweight request: 450 (prompt + response) -> baseline 1200 QPS minutes -> projected tokens/hour: 19.4M
- Avg tokens per long-context request: 3,800 -> baseline 35 RPS peak -> projected tokens/hour at peak: 480M
- Storage: KV cache retention per session ~12KB; expect cache warm hit rates 45–60% after 48h.

Operational notes
- Canary plan: start Tier B in hosted with autoscale and 2x burst buffer; after 2 weeks, enable Tier C only for tagged long-session traffic (route by header or routing key).
- Fallback: when capacity constrained, route long-context requests to a condensed prompt flow on Tier B with notification header to client.

Attachments: cp-model-compatibility.csv, peak-patterns-hourly.xlsx

Next steps:
1) Alyssa/Marcus: confirm p95 latency target (we assumed p95 <= 1.2s for Tier B in the sizing above).
2) Laura: please route any procurement/contact who will own the SLA to this thread.
3) We'll prepare an initial cost delta table for Tier A/B/C for the pilot sizing deck.

—Monica
Customer Success Engineer, Redwood Inference
